consumer_seed: The Ofcom mobile-switching guide was published on 1 October 2016.
The Ofcom mobile-switching guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Mobile customers can use the free Text to Switch process without speaking to their current provider.
A customer can text INFO to 85075 to check contract status and possible early termination charges.
A customer who wants to keep the mobile number can text PAC to 65075.
A customer who wants a new mobile number can text STAC to 75075.
The current provider must reply with a PAC or STAC switching code within one minute.
A PAC or STAC switching code is valid for 30 days.
Customers with more than one number on an account need to request the PAC or STAC by phone or through the provider website.
After receiving the PAC or STAC, the new provider must complete the mobile switch within one working day.
The old provider must not charge for a notice period after the mobile switching date.
A customer can keep an old mobile number for free after cancellation when the request is made within one month.
The Ofcom unwanted-calls services guide was published on 10 December 2013.
Caller display shows the number presented by the caller when it is available and the receiving phone has a display.
Caller-display information can support reporting, blocking and filtering of unwanted calls.
Number spoofing can cause a false or invalid telephone number to appear on caller display.
Incoming-call blocking services can prevent selected telephone numbers from getting through.
Some blocking products can route calls from a provider blocklist to junk voicemail.
Some blocking products can route calls that the customer has blocked to junk voicemail.
Some blocking products can filter calls with withheld numbers or international numbers.
Anonymous-call rejection can also block legitimate organisations that sometimes withhold their numbers, including emergency services and hospitals.
Dialling 1471 immediately after an unwanted call may identify the last caller unless the number was withheld.
Some mobile phones and third-party applications can identify suspected scam calls or screen calls.
The Ofcom number-portability information page was published on 3 April 2023.
Number portability is a regulated facility allowing customers to keep their numbers when changing provider.
Number portability supports consumer choice and competition by removing a barrier to switching.
Sections 51 and 58 of the Communications Act 2003 enable Ofcom to impose number-portability conditions.
Ofcom's provider rules for number portability and switching are set out in General Conditions B3 and C7.
Ofcom may enforce a breach of the relevant condition under sections 94 to 103 of the Communications Act 2003.
Civil proceedings for breach can require Ofcom consent under section 104 of the Communications Act 2003.
NICC, OTA2 and the Mobile Number Portability Operator Steering Group support technical and operational number-portability processes.
The Ofcom scam-protection guide was published on 15 July 2026.
The Ofcom scam-protection guide was last updated on 22 July 2026.
Ofcom advises people not to reply, click links, press buttons or share personal details when contact appears suspicious.
Ofcom advises checking for urgency, unexpected requests and suspicious links before acting.
Suspicious text messages can be forwarded to 7726 free of charge.
Scam calls can be reported to Report Fraud, or to Police Scotland in Scotland.
People should not give personal, banking, password or National Insurance details to unexpected callers.
A suspicious caller should be ended and the organisation contacted using a number from its official website or published information.
Ofcom advises not clicking links in unexpected text messages even when they appear to come from a recognised sender.
For a payment or login request, Ofcom advises visiting the organisation's website directly rather than using the supplied link.
A recipient can independently search a telephone number or sender name because other people may have reported it.
Many smartphones can block numbers, screen unknown callers or filter suspected spam calls.
Some providers offer network-level filtering that blocks known scam numbers before they reach the customer.
